objectives: Hear /b/ and /l/ in the correct order at the start of a word.
Blend initial /bl/ smoothly without inserting an extra vowel.
Identify and read familiar words beginning with bl.
Distinguish bl from similar beginnings such as b, br and fl.
concepts: A consonant blend contains two adjacent consonant phonemes; both sounds can be heard.
The onset is the beginning sound or sound group before the vowel and rime.
Smooth blending keeps consonants close together without adding an extra schwa vowel.
Accurate decoding uses every grapheme in sequence and then checks the whole word.

definitions.definition: Two or more adjacent consonant sounds in which each sound remains audible, such as /b/ and /l/ in black.
The consonant sound or consonant group at the beginning of a syllable, such as bl in block.
The vowel and any sounds that follow it in a syllable, such as -ock in block.
Joining phonemes closely in order without inserting extra vowel sounds.

workedExamples.solution: Keep /b/ and /l/ close, then blend /a/ and /k/: black.

workedExamples.prompt: Identify the onset and rime in block.
workedExamples.solution: The onset is bl; the rime is -ock.
Both begin with /b/, but black continues with /l/ and brick continues with /r/.
Remove the extra vowel and say /b/ /l/ smoothly before blending blue.

commonMistakes: Adding a vowel between /b/ and /l/, as in “buh-luh.”
Omitting /l/ and reading black as back.
Confusing bl with br because both start with /b/.
Guessing from the first letter without checking the full word.
keyTakeaways: In bl, hear /b/ followed by /l/; both sounds remain present.
Do not insert an extra vowel between the consonants.
Blend the whole word and check every sound.
Use the onset and rime to compare words while still reading each grapheme.
revisionPoints: Words: black, block, blob, blue, blink.
Smooth blending avoids an extra vowel between consonants.

conceptual.prompt: Why is bl called a consonant blend?
conceptual.answer: Both /b/ and /l/ can be heard in order.

conceptual.prompt: What is the onset in block?
What must you avoid when blending /b/ and /l/?
conceptual.answer: Adding an extra vowel between the consonants.

application.prompt: Which word starts with br instead of bl?

application.answer: Blend /b/ and /l/ smoothly to read black.

higherOrderThinking.prompt: How are black and block alike at the start?
How can you tell block from clock when decoding?
higherOrderThinking.answer: Check the first phoneme: block begins /b/ and clock begins /k/.

higherOrderThinking.prompt: Why is guessing from b alone not enough to read blue?
higherOrderThinking.answer: You must read the next consonant /l/ and the rest of the word.

quickRevision: Keep the two sounds close; do not add a vowel.
Blend the rest of the word and check every sound.
Compare onset and rime to read word families.

flashRecall.front: What is the initial blend in block?

flashRecall.back: The consonant sound or group at the beginning of a syllable.

flashRecall.front: What is the rime in block?
What should you avoid when blending bl?
flashRecall.back: Do not insert an extra vowel between /b/ and /l/.

formulaOrFactBank: black, block, blob, blue and blink begin with bl.
mistakeBasedRevision: If /l/ disappears, say both consonant sounds before blending the rest.
If an extra vowel appears, shorten the gap between /b/ and /l/.
If bl and br are confused, contrast block with brick and identify the second consonant.
weakTopicRevision: If initial-bl accuracy is weak, practise listening contrasts, model continuous blending, sort bl/br/fl words, and reassess with fresh examples.

activities.name: Build and blend four-sound bl-words.
steps: Place one counter for each phoneme in black, block and blob.
Say /b/ then /l/ without an added vowel.
Blend through the vowel and final consonant.
Read the whole word and check each sound.

activities.name: Sort bl-words by onset and rime.
steps: Sort black, block, blob, blue and blink under the onset bl.
Group block with sock by the -ock rime while noting the different onsets.
Contrast block and brick to hear /l/ versus /r/.
Explain how the sound evidence supports each sort.

outcomes: Identify /b/ followed by /l/ at the beginning of a taught word.
Blend familiar initial-bl words without inserting an extra vowel.
Read each grapheme in sequence and self-correct an omitted consonant.
Use onset and rime to compare taught words.
